# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy to New Billing System

## Overview
Both billing systems will run in parallel throughout the migration, allowing safe rollback at any point before full cutover. Users are migrated in batches based on risk profile (internal/test accounts first, then increasing cohorts of real customers), with strict entry criteria gating progression between phases.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (Internal & Low-Risk Accounts)
**Scope:** 2% of users (~800 accounts) — internal test accounts, employee accounts, and opted-in low-ARR customers.

**Entry Criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end parallel invoice reconciliation testing against the old system for 2 consecutive billing cycles with 100% invoice-amount parity on a synthetic dataset, and rollback procedure has been dry-run successfully at least once.

**Activities:** Migrate accounts, run both systems in parallel (old system remains source of truth for actual charges), compare outputs daily, fix discrepancies.

---

## Phase 2: Early Adopters (Expanded Cohort)
**Scope:** 18% of users (~7,200 accounts, cumulative 20%) — mix of plan types, geographies, and payment methods (credit card, ACH, invoice-billed) to surface edge cases.

**Entry Criterion:** Phase 1 completed with zero critical (Sev-1/Sev-2) billing defects open for 14 consecutive days, invoice discrepancy rate ≤ 0.1% of Phase 1 accounts, and customer support ticket volume related to billing for migrated accounts within 1.5x of baseline (non-migrated) ticket rate.

**Activities:** New system becomes source of truth for these accounts' actual charges; old system kept live and synced read-only for audit/rollback. Expand monitoring dashboards and support runbooks.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability Rollout
**Scope:** 60% of users (~24,000 accounts, cumulative 80%) — remaining general population, migrated in weekly waves of ~10-15% to control blast radius.

**Entry Criterion:** Phase 2 completed with invoice discrepancy rate ≤ 0.05%, no unresolved Sev-1 incidents, payment failure rate for migrated accounts within 0.5 percentage points of the old system's baseline failure rate, and finance sign-off on reconciliation process at this scale.

**Activities:** Automated migration tooling runs in scheduled waves; old system remains fully operational in parallel as fallback for each wave for a minimum 7-day soak period before the next wave starts.

---

## Phase 4: Final Batch & Stabilization
**Scope:** Remaining 20% of users (~8,000 accounts, cumulative 100%) — highest-risk/complex accounts (custom contracts, enterprise/multi-entity billing, accounts with active disputes).

**Entry Criterion:** Phase 3 completed with cumulative discrepancy rate ≤ 0.05%, zero open Sev-1 incidents for 21 consecutive days, and dedicated migration support plan approved for enterprise accounts (white-glove handling, account manager notification).

**Activities:** Migrate final batch with enhanced monitoring and dedicated support coverage. **Old billing system remains fully active and untouched during this phase** — no deletion, disabling, or decommissioning occurs until a separate, subsequent decommissioning phase (Phase 5, not covered here) after a full billing-cycle stabilization period (minimum 30 days) confirms 100% parity with zero critical issues across all migrated accounts.

---

## Risks

RISK: Invoice amount discrepancies between old and new systems cause customer billing disputes | Run parallel reconciliation reports daily during each phase and auto-flag any variance above 0.1% for manual review before customer-facing charges are finalized | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: Payment gateway/tokenization mismatch causes failed or duplicate charges during cutover | Migrate stored payment methods via a validated tokenization bridge and require a successful $0 authorization check per account before live billing switches over | Payments Platform Team
RISK: Data migration script silently drops or corrupts subscription/proration data for complex accounts | Require automated schema validation and row-count/checksum reconciliation post-migration for every batch, with a hard block on wave progression until validation passes | Data Migration Engineer
RISK: Customer support is overwhelmed by billing-related tickets during a wave, masking a systemic defect | Set a per-wave ticket-volume alert threshold and pause new migrations if triggered until root cause is triaged | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Rollback path degrades or is untested at scale, leaving no safe fallback if a major defect is found late | Conduct a full rollback rehearsal before each phase and keep the old system as the system of record until each cohort's soak period completes | Site Reliability Engineering Lead

## Halt Criteria (Metric Threshold)
If the invoice discrepancy rate for any actively migrating cohort exceeds **0.5%** of invoices in a single billing cycle, or the payment failure rate for migrated accounts exceeds the pre-migration baseline by more than **2 percentage points**, the rollout is immediately halted, no further accounts are migrated, and the incident is escalated to the Billing Engineering Lead and SRE Lead for root-cause analysis before any wave resumes.

PHASES: 4
